questions.question: The length of a Gunter's chain is:
questions.questionMalayalam: ഗുണ്ടേഴ്സ് ചെയിനിന്റെ നീളം എത്രയാണ്?
questions.explanation: Gunter's chain has 100 links and total length of 66 feet (20.12 m). 10 Gunter chains = 1 Furlong, 80 Gunter chains = 1 Mile, 10 square Gunter chains = 1 Acre.

questions.question: In a prismatic compass, the zero of the graduated ring is marked at the:
questions.questionMalayalam: പ്രിസ്മാറ്റിക് കോമ്പസിൽ പൂജ്യം ഡിഗ്രി (0°) അടയാളപ്പെടുത്തിയിരിക്കുന്നത് ഏത് ദിശയിലാണ്?
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° (or 360°) is marked at the SOUTH end, 90° at West, 180° at North, and 270° at East because readings are viewed through the prism at the South end while sighting the object at North.

questions.question: If the Fore Bearing (FB) of a line AB is 45° 30', then its Back Bearing (BB) is:
questions.questionMalayalam: ഒരു ലൈനിന്റെ Fore Bearing 45° 30' ആണെങ്കിൽ, അതിന്റെ Back Bearing എത്ര?
questions.explanation: Formula: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since FB (45° 30') < 180°, BB = 45° 30' + 180° = 225° 30'.

questions.question: The correction for sag in a surveying tape is always:
questions.questionMalayalam: ടേപ്പിലെ സാഗ് കറക്ഷൻ (Sag Correction) എപ്പോഴും:
questions.explanation: Because a suspended tape sags under its own weight into a catenary curve, the measured distance is always greater than the true straight line distance. Hence sag correction is ALWAYS SUBTRACTIVE (-ve).

questions.question: Which section of Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act 1961 deals with the notification of completion of survey?
questions.questionMalayalam: കേരള സർവേ & അതിരടയാള നിയമം 1961 പ്രകാരം സർവേ പൂർത്തീകരണ വിജ്ഞാപനം ഏത് വകുപ്പാണ്?
questions.explanation: Section 13 of the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act 1961 mandates the publication of the final notification when survey is completed.

questions.question: Reciprocal levelling eliminates which of the following errors?
questions.questionMalayalam: റെസിപ്രോക്കൽ ലെവലിങ് വഴി പൂർണ്ണമായി ഒഴിവാക്കാവുന്ന പിശകുകൾ ഏതെല്ലാം?
options: Earth curvature and atmospheric refraction only
Collimation error, earth curvature and atmospheric refraction
Index error and parallax error only
questions.explanation: Reciprocal levelling eliminates: (1) Error due to instrument collimation line not being horizontal, (2) Error due to curvature of the earth, (3) Error due to uniform atmospheric refraction.

questions.question: The multiplying constant (k) for an anallatic tacheometer is:
questions.questionMalayalam: അനലാറ്റിക് ടക്കിയോമീറ്ററിലെ മൾട്ടിപ്ലൈയിംഗ് കോൺസ്റ്റന്റ് (k) എത്രയാണ്?
questions.explanation: For a standard tacheometer, Multiplying constant k = f / i = 100. For an anallatic telescope fitted with an internal anallatic lens, Additive constant c = (f + d) = 0.

questions.question: In AutoCad, which function key toggles Ortho mode ON and OFF?
questions.questionMalayalam: ഓട്ടോകോഡിൽ ഓർത്തോ മോഡ് (Ortho Mode) ഓൺ/ഓഫ് ചെയ്യാനുള്ള ഫംഗ്ഷൻ കീ ഏതാണ്?
questions.explanation: F8 toggles Ortho mode (locks cursor movement to 90° horizontal/vertical). F3 is OSNAP, F7 is Grid, F9 is Snap.

questions.question: When a staff is held on the soffit (underside) of a bridge deck, the reading is recorded as:
questions.questionMalayalam: പാലത്തിന്റെ അടിഭാഗത്ത് സ്റ്റാഫ് തലതിരിച്ച് പിടിച്ച് റീഡിംഗ് എടുക്കുമ്പോൾ അതിനെ എങ്ങനെ അടയാളപ്പെടുത്തുന്നു?
questions.explanation: Inverted staff reading is taken when the staff base is placed against a high ceiling/soffit. In the levelling field book, it is entered with a minus sign (-). RL of Soffit = HI + (- Staff Reading) = HI - Staff Reading.

questions.questionMalayalam: കേരള സർവേ വകുപ്പിൽ FMB പ്ലോട്ടുകൾ വരയ്ക്കാൻ സാധാരണയായി ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്ന സ്കെയിൽ ഏത്?
questions.explanation: In Kerala Cadastral Survey, FMB (Field Measurement Book) sketches are drafted at 1:1000 or 1:2000 scale depending on the parcel size and village map specifications.

questions.question: Total Station uses which electromagnetic wave carrier for EDM measurement?
questions.questionMalayalam: ടോട്ടൽ സ്റ്റേഷനിലെ EDM അളവുകൾക്കായി ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്ന ഇലക്ട്രോമാഗ്നറ്റിക് തരംഗങ്ങൾ ഏവ?
options: Infrared / Modulated Light waves or Microwave

Evaluated under authentic Kerala PSC pattern (-0.33 negative marking).

questions.question: When the line of sight is perpendicular to the horizontal axis the vertical circle must read:
questions.explanation: When the line of sight is perpendicular to the horizontal axis and truly horizontal, the vertical circle must read 0° 0' 0". Any discrepancy is known as index error.
questions.rankerTip: Vertical circle reads 0° when the line of sight is horizontal.

questions.question: What test is that the vertical circle indicate zero while the line of sight is perpendicular to the vertical axis in theodolite?
questions.explanation: The Vertical Arc Test is the permanent adjustment test ensuring that the vertical circle vernier reads zero when the telescope bubble is centered and line of sight is horizontal.
questions.rankerTip: Vertical arc test = Ensures vertical circle reads zero when line of sight is horizontal.

questions.question: What is used as horizontal arm in vernier frame of theodolite instrument?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Index arm'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Index arm.

questions.question: The imaginary line joining the centre at the eye piece and optical centre of the objective in a theodolite is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Axis of telescope'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Axis of telescope.

questions.question: Which method is rarely used in theodolite traverse survey as it is prone to local attraction?
questions.explanation: The loose needle method determines magnetic bearings independently at each station using a magnetic compass needle, making it prone to local attraction errors.
questions.rankerTip: Loose needle method is prone to local attraction.

questions.question: Face left and face right observations are connected with
questions.explanation: Face left and face right observations are uniquely connected with theodolite observations to eliminate systematic instrumental errors.
questions.rankerTip: Face left & face right = Theodolite surveying technique.
questions.topic: Face Left and Face Right Observations

questions.question: Which method is suitable for closed traverse in theodolite survey?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Included angle method'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Included angle method.

questions.question: Accurate centering of theodolite can be done easily by
options: With the help of tripod legs
questions.explanation: A shifting head allows the theodolite to be moved horizontally over the tripod head by a few centimetres for rapid and exact centering over the station peg.
questions.rankerTip: Shifting head = Quick, fine centering over the ground mark.

questions.question: The size of theodolite is specified by
questions.explanation: The size of a transit theodolite is designated by the diameter of the graduated circle on its lower plate (e.g., a 15 cm theodolite has a 15 cm diameter lower scale plate).
questions.rankerTip: Size of theodolite = Diameter of the graduated circle of the lower plate.

questions.question: What is the method of prolongation of a straight line that result cumulative errors, if the instrument is not in adjustment?
options: Prolonging a line by first method
Prolonging a line by second method
Prolonging a line by third method
Prolonging a line by fourth method
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Prolonging a line by first method'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Prolonging a line by first method.
questions.topic: Errors and Accuracies in Theodolite Surveying

questions.question: When the cross hairs are not clearly visible ?
options: The cross hairs should be adjusted
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Eye piece should be focussed'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Eye piece should be focussed.

questions.question: What is referred to smallest measureable unit in theodolite?
questions.explanation: The smallest unit that can be measured directly using the vernier of a theodolite is termed its least count.
questions.rankerTip: Smallest measurable unit = Least count (20").

questions.question: The upper plate of a theodolite is fixed to
questions.explanation: The upper plate (vernier plate carrying verniers A and B) is attached to the inner solid spindle, while the lower scale plate is attached to the outer hollow spindle.
questions.rankerTip: Upper plate = Inner solid spindle; Lower plate = Outer hollow spindle.

questions.question: How many methods are there to measure horizontal angle in theodolite?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is '3 methods'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: 3 methods.

questions.question: What is the term, if the angle between the line of sight and a horizontal line at a station in theodolite survey?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Vertical angle'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Vertical angle.

questions.question: An internal focusing type of telescope the lens provided as
questions.explanation: In an internal focusing telescope, an internal double-concave lens is moved along the longitudinal axis between the objective and eyepiece.
questions.rankerTip: Internal focusing telescope uses a movable concave lens.

questions.question: The process of establishing intermediate points between two end points which are not intervisible, with the help of a theodolite is called
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Balancing-in'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Balancing-in.

questions.question: SPIRE TEST is used in permanent adjustment of theodolite for adjusting the
questions.explanation: The Spire Test is used in the permanent adjustment of a theodolite to make the horizontal (trunnion) axis perpendicular to the vertical axis.
questions.rankerTip: Spire Test = Adjusts horizontal axis perpendicular to vertical axis.

questions.question: Which method without transiting gives the best results even while the theodolite instrument is not in perfect adjustment by traverse survey?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Direct method'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Direct method.

questions.question: How to eliminate error while plate level axis not being perpendicular to vertical axis in theodolite?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'By permanent adjustment'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: By permanent adjustment.
questions.topic: Errors and Accuracies in Theodolite Surveying

questions.question: Axis about which telescope of theodolite can be rotated in horizontal plane is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Vertical axis'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Vertical axis.

questions.question: The difference between the most probable value of a quantity and its observed value is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Residual error'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Residual error.

questions.question: What test is that the line of sight perpendicular to the horizontal axis in theodolite?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Collimation test'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Collimation test.

questions.question: The line passing through the centres of curvature of the faces of lens is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Principle axis'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Principle axis.

questions.question: What is the term, if the angle is measured below the horizontal line in theodolite survey?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Angle of depression'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Angle of depression.

questions.question: When the bubble of a level tube is at the centre of its run :
options: Geometrical axis of the telescope is horizontal
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Line of sight is horizontal'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Line of sight is horizontal.

questions.question: What is the term, if the angle between the prolongation of preceding and succeeding line?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Deflection angle'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Deflection angle.

questions.question: The absence of Chromatic Aberration is known as
questions.explanation: Achromatism is the freedom of a lens system from chromatic aberration (the dispersion of white light into constituent colours).
questions.rankerTip: Achromatism = Freedom from chromatic aberration.

questions.question: In Theodolite traversing method consists in measuring the several angles successively and finally closing the horizon at the starting point
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Reiteration method'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Reiteration method.

questions.question: The imaginary line joining the point of inter section of cross hair at diaphragm and the optical centre of the object glass and its continuation is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Line of collimation'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Line of collimation.

questions.question: The fine adjustments in theodolite is done by :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Tangent screw'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Tangent screw.

questions.question: Face left and face right observation eliminate ______ error
questions.explanation: Taking the mean of face left and face right vertical angle observations completely eliminates index error of the vertical circle.
questions.rankerTip: Face left + Face right eliminates index error, collimation error, and horizontal axis tilt error.
questions.topic: Face Left and Face Right Observations

questions.question: What is the variation of direct angle?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is '0° to 360°'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: 0° to 360°.

questions.question: Which method, the error is not carried over to the other span in prolonging line by theodolite?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Methods II'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Methods II.
questions.topic: Errors and Accuracies in Theodolite Surveying

questions.question: Direct angle obtained from theodolite may between :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is '0 - 360°'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.

questions.question: The instrument used for orienting plane table is
options: Both Trough compass and Circular or box compass
questions.explanation: A trough compass is used to find and mark the magnetic north meridian on the drawing sheet for preliminary or rough orientation.
questions.rankerTip: Trough compass establishes the magnetic meridian direction on the drawing sheet.

questions.question: Process of orientation means setting up the table
questions.explanation: Process of orientation means setting the table at successive stations such that its plotted north-south lines remain parallel to the meridian.
questions.rankerTip: Orientation sets the table parallel to the meridian (or base line).

questions.question: Instrument used for sighting objects and drawing rays in plane tabling is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Alidade'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Alidade.

questions.question: Triangle of error is formed in which of the following methods?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Lehman's Method'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Lehman's Method.

questions.question: How many methods are used to solve by three point problem?
questions.explanation: The three-point problem can be solved by three main classes of methods: (1) Mechanical (tracing paper), (2) Graphical (Bessel's), and (3) Trial and error (Lehmann's).
questions.rankerTip: 3 main methods to solve 3-point problem: Mechanical, Graphical, and Trial & Error.

questions.question: The field work and office work are done simultaneously in
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Plane table survey'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Plane table survey.

questions.question: What is the name of method used in plane table survey similar to that of compass survey or theodolite?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Traversing'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Traversing.

questions.question: In setting up a plane table at any station
options: Both levelling and centering are done simultaneously
questions.explanation: In setting up a plane table at any station, levelling and centering are carried out almost simultaneously, followed by orientation.
questions.rankerTip: Order of setup: Levelling & Centering (simultaneously) -> Orientation.

mockTests.title: Levelling 187 MCQ Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Comprehensive 187-question examination covering all core aspects of Levelling: Principles, Instruments (Dumpy, Tilting, Reversible, Auto & Digital Levels), Levelling Staves, Reductions (HI & Rise and Fall), Reciprocal Levelling, Errors, Corrections (Curvature & Refraction), and Benchmarks. Evaluated under authentic Kerala PSC pattern (-0.33 negative marking).

questions.question: Which instrument may compute and apply refraction and curvature corrections?
questions.explanation: Modern electronic / digital levels equipped with microprocessor control and barcode sensors automatically compute and apply both earth curvature and atmospheric refraction corrections internally.
questions.rankerTip: Digital levels automatically apply earth curvature and refraction corrections to staff readings.

questions.question: When the bubble is in the centre of the bubble tube, the bubble line is :
questions.explanation: When the bubble of the level tube is centered, the bubble axis (tangent to the longitudinal curve at center) is perfectly horizontal.
questions.rankerTip: Centered bubble = Bubble line / axis is horizontal.

questions.question: A staff reading taken on a point whose elevation is to be determined as on a change point is called :
questions.explanation: A Fore Sight (FS) is the last staff reading taken from an instrument station before shifting the level, or the final sight taken on a point whose elevation is to be determined.
questions.rankerTip: Fore Sight (FS) = Last reading before shifting; Back Sight (BS) = First reading after setting up.

questions.question: What is reduced level, if height of line of collimation is 98.717m and inter sight is 1.238m?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is '97.479m'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: 97.479m.

questions.question: Height of instrument method the leveling is compared to rise and fall method is
questions.explanation: The Height of Collimation (HI) method is quicker and less tedious than the Rise and Fall method when there are numerous intermediate sights, though it provides no arithmetic check on intermediate sights.
questions.rankerTip: HI method = Faster for many intermediate sights; Rise & Fall = Thorough check on all sights (BS, IS, FS).

questions.question: To avoid instrumental error, the length of the back sight and fore sight are kept
options: Kept length of BS more than FS
questions.explanation: To avoid instrumental errors (such as collimation error) as well as earth curvature and average refraction errors, the lengths of back sight and fore sight should be kept equal.
questions.rankerTip: Equal BS and FS distances automatically eliminate collimation error and curvature/refraction errors.

questions.question: What is the level that combine good features both the dumpy level and 'y' level?
questions.explanation: Cooke's reversible level combines the rigidity of a Dumpy level with the reversibility of a Wye level. The telescope can be rotated 180° inside its socket to eliminate collimation errors.
questions.rankerTip: Cooke's reversible level combines features of Dumpy and Y-level and eliminates collimation error.

questions.question: The main function of levelling is
options: To prepare a plan or map
To determine the elevations of the points
To calculate the volume of earthwork
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'To determine the elevations of the points'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: To determine the elevations of the points.

questions.question: What is the term of sight, if the sight taken between the back sight and fore sight on a levelling staff held over a point ofunknown elevations?
questions.explanation: An Intermediate Sight (IS) is any staff reading taken on a point of unknown elevation between the Back Sight and the Fore Sight from the same instrument setup.
questions.rankerTip: Intermediate Sight (IS) = Any reading between BS and FS from the same setup.

questions.question: Which instrument is mainly designed for precise levelling work?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Tilting level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Tilting level.

questions.question: A reference surface above which elevation of a point are determined is called a ______ surface
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Datum'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Datum.

questions.question: The smallest reading that can be measured by using levelling staff is :
questions.explanation: The least count of a standard metric levelling staff is 5 mm (0.005 m). Each black and white strip graduation has a height of 5 mm.
questions.rankerTip: Least count of standard metric levelling staff = 5 mm (0.005 m).

questions.question: What is the name of level, if the fly levelling done at the end of day's work to connect the finishing point with the starting point on that particular day?
questions.explanation: Check levelling is a form of fly levelling conducted at the end of a day's work from the finishing point back to the starting benchmark to check the accuracy of the day's levelling.
questions.rankerTip: Check levelling connects the day's finishing point back to the starting point to detect closing errors.

questions.question: What bench mark is established for short duration such as at the end of a days work?
questions.explanation: A Temporary Bench Mark (TBM) is established at the end of a day's work on a stable object to resume levelling the next morning from that exact reference point.
questions.rankerTip: Temporary BM (TBM) is set at the end of a working day to resume work next morning.

questions.question: When viewed through a telescope the staff reading is seen :
questions.explanation: An inverted staff reading is taken when the bottom of a structure (such as a bridge girder, tunnel roof, beam soffit, or lintel) is above the instrument line of sight. In level book entries, it is recorded with a negative sign.
questions.rankerTip: Inverted staff reading = Point is ABOVE the line of collimation (entered as negative in level book).

questions.question: What is name of the level which does not required any protection from the sun?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Auto level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Auto level.

questions.question: The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Intermediate sights'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Intermediate sights.

questions.question: What is the another name of positive or plus sight in levelling survey?
questions.explanation: A Back Sight (BS) is the first staff reading taken after setting up the levelling instrument, taken on a point of known elevation (Benchmark or Change Point). It is also called a plus sight.
questions.rankerTip: Back sight (BS) is always the FIRST reading taken from any instrument position and is ADDED to RL to get HI.

questions.question: In one setting up of the level the maximum number of back sight and fore sight is
questions.explanation: In any single setting up of the level, there can be at most one Back Sight (the first reading) and one Fore Sight (the final reading before shifting).
questions.rankerTip: Every setup has exactly ONE Back Sight and at most ONE Fore Sight.

questions.question: Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated By ______ of level tube
questions.explanation: The sensitiveness of a level tube increases with an increase in the radius of curvature of the internal surface of the tube, increase in tube diameter, increase in bubble length, and decrease in liquid viscosity and surface tension.
questions.rankerTip: Sensitivity increases with: (1) Larger radius R, (2) Larger diameter, (3) Longer bubble, (4) Lower viscosity/surface tension.

questions.question: What type of staff is used, if the sight are long?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Target staff'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Target staff.

questions.question: Levelling carried out along the given route to find the elevations of points at known distance is called
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Profile levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Profile levelling.

questions.question: The error due to refraction and curvature are avoids in :
questions.explanation: Reciprocal levelling completely eliminates the error due to earth curvature and atmospheric refraction (assuming refraction remains constant during the observations).
questions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling eliminates curvature, collimation error, and uniform refraction errors across obstacles.

questions.question: In a perfect check leveling the result of arithmetic check is always
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Zero'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Zero.

questions.question: Tilting levels are used as
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Precise leveling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Precise leveling.

questions.question: Combined correction for curvature and refraction is
questions.explanation: The combined correction for curvature and refraction is Cc - Cr = 0.0785 D² - 0.0112 D² = 0.0673 D² metres (where D is distance in kilometres). It is always subtractive from staff readings.
questions.rankerTip: Combined correction = 0.0673 D² m (subtractive); Curvature = 0.0785 D² m (-); Refraction = 0.0112 D² m (+).

questions.question: What is the process if the difference of level between two points is determined by setting the levelling instrument midway between the point?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Simple levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Simple levelling.

questions.question: What is the distance of interval all over country with respect to the mean sea level of Mumbai as datum?
questions.explanation: Primary GTS bench marks across the country are established at approximately 100 km intervals.
questions.rankerTip: Primary GTS benchmarks were established at ~100 km intervals.

questions.question: When the length of sight is more than 100m the staff used is called
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Target staff'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Target staff.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'BS + FS = HI'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: BS + FS = HI.

questions.question: The still water surface of a pond represent a ______ surface
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level.

questions.question: A levelling instrument, consisting a telescope attached with level tube which can be tilted within few degrees in a vertical plane by a tilting screw is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'The tilting level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: The tilting level.

questions.question: The bench marks used in small levelling are
questions.explanation: An Arbitrary (or Assumed) Bench Mark is a reference point whose elevation is arbitrarily assumed (e.g. +100.000 m or +50.000 m) for small, localized levelling operations where actual MSL is not essential.
questions.rankerTip: Arbitrary BM = Assumed datum (e.g. 100.00 m) for localized surveys.

questions.question: Which levelling is adopted if there is obstacles between the points?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Differential levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Differential levelling.

questions.question: What is the deflection angle that the angle measured in clockwise direction?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Right deflection angle'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Right deflection angle.

questions.question: The method of surveying used for determining the relative heights of points on the surface of the earth is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Levelling.

questions.question: What is the message to indicate the movement of left arm over 90°?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Move my left'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Move my left.

questions.question: In ______ type level, the line of collimation is not at right angles to the vertical axis if the instrument is permanent adjustment
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Tilting level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Tilting level.

questions.question: Levelling should always commence from a :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Bench mark'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Bench mark.

questions.question: In a level tube, the larger the radius of curvature, the sensitiveness is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Greater'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Greater.

questions.question: If a point sighted is above the horizontal axis, then the vertical axis is known as:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Angle of Elevation'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Angle of Elevation.

questions.question: The error in leveling operation during settlement of tripod on turning point is
questions.explanation: Settlement of the tripod feet into soft ground at turning points is classified as a natural/environmental source of error occurring during field operations.
questions.rankerTip: Tripod settlement in soft turf/sand = Natural/site error; use firm turning pins to avoid.

questions.question: Sensitiveness of bubble tube increased by :
options: Increase in the length of bubble
questions.explanation: Sensitiveness of the bubble tube is increased by increasing the length of bubble, increasing internal diameter, increasing radius of curvature, and decreasing liquid viscosity.
questions.rankerTip: All factors that reduce resistance or increase curvature radius increase bubble tube sensitiveness.

questions.question: The height of instrument method is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'All of these'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: All of these.

questions.question: What is the position of line of collimation While the observed reading is the less than the required true reading?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Inclined downwards'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Inclined downwards.

questions.question: The point on which both back sight and fore sight are taken :
questions.explanation: A Change Point (CP) or Turning Point (TP) is a station point denoting the shifting of the levelling instrument, upon which both Fore Sight (from old setup) and Back Sight (from new setup) are taken.
questions.rankerTip: On a change point (CP), two sights are taken: FS (to close old setup) and BS (to start new setup).

questions.question: Reduced level is also known as
questions.explanation: Reduced Level (RL) of a point is its vertical distance (elevation) above or below the chosen datum surface.
questions.rankerTip: RL = Elevation of the point with reference to datum.

questions.question: Permanent adjustment of a level are
questions.explanation: The correct answer is '2 in number'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: 2 in number.

questions.question: In a bubble tube the length of one division is :
questions.explanation: The standard length of one graduation (division) on a level tube is 2 mm (0.1 inch in older standards).
questions.rankerTip: Standard bubble tube division length = 2 mm.

questions.question: Profile levelling is usually done for determining
questions.explanation: Profile levelling (longitudinal sectioning) is carried out along the centerline of a proposed route (road, railway, canal, pipeline) to determine ground undulations and design gradients.
questions.rankerTip: Profile levelling determines elevations along a route alignment to obtain the longitudinal profile.

questions.question: A surface which is normal to the direction of gravity at all points, as indicated by a plumb line, is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level surface'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level surface.

questions.question: When focusing object glass, telescope is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Directed to object'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Directed to object.

questions.question: The operation of levelling to determining the elevation of points some distance apart or to establish bench marks is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Differential levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Differential levelling.

questions.question: Rise and fall method is used for :
questions.explanation: The Rise and Fall method is used for reducing levels from field book staff readings by calculating the difference in level between consecutive points.
questions.rankerTip: Rise and Fall method determines differential elevation changes between consecutive staff positions.

questions.question: The average level taken up by the sea in all states of the oscillation is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Mean sea level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Mean sea level.

questions.question: According to BIS, the length of folding staff is ______ meter
questions.explanation: A telescopic metric staff consists of three slide-in extendable lengths (often extending to 4 metres total length) that slide into each other for compact transport.
questions.rankerTip: Telescopic staff has 3 extendable sliding sections, total length 4 m (bottom 1.5m, middle 1.25m, top 1.25m).

questions.question: What is the adjustment done to place the vertical axis exactly over the station?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Centering'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Centering.

questions.question: What formula is used with arithmetical check in height of collimation method?
options: ΣB.S - ΣF.S = Last R.L - First R.L
ΣB.S + ΣF.S = Last R.L - First R.L
B.S - F.S = Last R.L - First R.L
ΣB.S + ΣF.S = Rise - Fall = Last R.L - First R.L
questions.explanation: In the Height of Collimation method, the arithmetical check is: ΣBS - ΣFS = Last RL - First RL. It does not check intermediate sight calculations.
questions.rankerTip: HI method check: ΣBS - ΣFS = Last RL - First RL.

questions.question: Which line is normal to plumb line at all points?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level line'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level line.

questions.question: A staff reading taken on a bench mark or change point is known as :
questions.explanation: A Back Sight (BS) is the first staff reading taken after setting up the levelling instrument, taken on a point of known elevation (Benchmark or Change Point). It is also called a plus sight.
questions.rankerTip: Back sight (BS) is always the FIRST reading taken from any instrument position and is ADDED to RL to get HI.

questions.question: The line lying on a level surface and normal to the plumb line is
questions.explanation: A level surface is everywhere perpendicular (normal) to the plumb line (direction of gravity).

questions.question: What is the folded length of staff, while folding staff is not in use?

questions.rankerTip: Folding staff: Total length = 4 m; Folded length = 2 m.

questions.question: In which staff consist of three parts and one slides into another?

questions.question: The following sights are taken on a turning point

questions.question: In which type of level the collimation error is eliminated?

questions.question: The datum adopted for establishing GTS bench mark :

questions.question: The number of fundamental lines for dumpy level is
questions.explanation: A Dumpy level has 4 fundamental lines: (1) Line of collimation, (2) Axis of the telescope, (3) Axis of the bubble tube, and (4) Vertical axis.
questions.rankerTip: Four fundamental lines in Dumpy level: Collimation line, Telescope axis, Bubble tube axis, Vertical axis.

questions.question: The bench mark established by the survey of India department with very high precision with reference to mean sea levelat Mumbai as the datum are called
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'G.T.S. Bench Marks'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: G.T.S. Bench Marks.

questions.question: Sensitivity of Level tubes can be increased by

questions.question: Collimation line is

questions.question: The vertical distance above or below the datum is ______ of a point.

questions.question: The level designated as self aligning level :

questions.question: Which one is, in the following that does not have the object of levelling ?

questions.question: System of levelling chiefly employed for establishing bench marks with high precision is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Precise levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Precise levelling.

questions.question: The sensitiveness of a level tube decreases, if
options: Radius of curvature of its inner surface is increased
Diameter of the tube is increased
Length of the vapour is increased
Both viscosity and surface tension are increased
questions.explanation: Sensitiveness decreases when viscosity and surface tension of the bubble liquid increase, as this impedes smooth bubble movement.
questions.rankerTip: Higher viscosity and surface tension = Decreased bubble sensitiveness.

questions.question: Dumpy level is fixed in between the stations A and B. The staff reading on A is 2.65 m and that on B is 1.5m. Then the ground is
questions.explanation: An Intermediate Sight (IS) is any staff reading taken on a point of unknown elevation between the Back Sight and the Fore Sight from the same instrument setup.
questions.rankerTip: Intermediate Sight (IS) = Any reading between BS and FS from the same setup.

questions.question: What is the level that is widely used in construction work but not for more precise control work?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Laser level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Laser level.

questions.question: The permissible closing error for accurate levelling is expressed as
questions.explanation: The permissible closing error in accurate levelling is E = ± 0.012 √K metres (where K is the distance levelled in kilometres).
questions.rankerTip: Closing error limits: Rough = ± 0.100 √K; Ordinary = ± 0.025 √K; Accurate = ± 0.012 √K; Precise = ± 0.006 √K.

questions.question: A level surface is
questions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface concentric with the mean spheroidal surface of the earth, normal to the direction of gravity (plumb line) at every point. A level line is a line lying in a level surface.
questions.rankerTip: Level surface/line is CURVED and concentric with Earth; Horizontal line is STRAIGHT and tangential to level line.

questions.question: Which levelling rod is used for precise work?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Invar staff'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Invar staff.

questions.question: The branch of surveying which deals with the measurement in vertical plane is known as:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Levelling.

questions.question: A first sight taken on a levelling staff held at a point of known elevation is termed as
questions.explanation: A Back Sight (BS) is the first staff reading taken after setting up the levelling instrument, taken on a point of known elevation (Benchmark or Change Point). It is also called a plus sight.
questions.rankerTip: Back sight (BS) is always the FIRST reading taken from any instrument position and is ADDED to RL to get HI.

questions.question: Focussing the eye-piece and object glass in temporary adjustments of a level is performed to :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Eliminate parallax error'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Eliminate parallax error.

questions.question: What is the full form of GTS?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Great trigonometrical survey'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Great trigonometrical survey.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an indirect levelling method ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Trigonometric levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Trigonometric levelling.

questions.question: What is the benchmarks established between the G.T.S. benchmarks by the state PWD is known as
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Permanent benchmark'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Permanent benchmark.

questions.question: The sights which are taken on turning point :
questions.explanation: A Fore Sight (FS) is the last staff reading taken from an instrument station before shifting the level, or the final sight taken on a point whose elevation is to be determined.
questions.rankerTip: Fore Sight (FS) = Last reading before shifting; Back Sight (BS) = First reading after setting up.

questions.question: To set the eye piece and object glass at the proper distance apart for the clear vision of the object sighted, the process isknown :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Focusing'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Focusing.

questions.question: Which column is used for last entry on the level book page?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Fore sight'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Fore sight.

questions.question: Leveling across a river is done by
questions.explanation: Reciprocal levelling is employed when levelling across wide obstacles (rivers, ravines, lakes) where the instrument cannot be placed midway. Two sets of readings taken from both banks eliminate curvature, collimation, and average refraction errors.
questions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling across rivers eliminates curvature error, collimation error, and uniform refraction error.

questions.question: The first step in levelling process is to find
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'The height of instrument'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: The height of instrument.

questions.question: What is the term that is normal to plumb line at all points?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level surface'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level surface.

questions.question: In levelling, a station point where :
questions.explanation: An Intermediate Sight (IS) is any staff reading taken on a point of unknown elevation between the Back Sight and the Fore Sight from the same instrument setup.
questions.rankerTip: Intermediate Sight (IS) = Any reading between BS and FS from the same setup.

questions.question: How the staff should be read?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Upwards'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Upwards.

questions.question: Diaphragm of a survey telescope is held inside
options: Telescope tube at its end nearer the eye piece
Telescope tube at its mid point
questions.explanation: The diaphragm holding the crosshairs is fitted inside the telescope tube just in front of the eyepiece, at the focal plane of the objective.
questions.rankerTip: Crosshairs / Diaphragm are fitted directly in front of the eyepiece.

questions.question: In metric levelling staff, number of subdivisions per meter length are
questions.explanation: Since each graduation division on a metric staff is 5 mm, there are 1000 mm / 5 mm = 200 subdivisions per metre length.
questions.rankerTip: Number of 5 mm subdivisions per metre of staff = 1000 / 5 = 200 divisions.

questions.question: Which levelling is done to connect the B.M to any intermediate point of the alignment for checking the accuracy of thework?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Fly levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Fly levelling.

questions.question: In the surveying telescopes, cross hairs are fitted in
options: Optical centre of the eye piece
questions.explanation: The diaphragm holding the crosshairs is fitted inside the telescope tube just in front of the eyepiece, at the focal plane of the objective.
questions.rankerTip: Crosshairs / Diaphragm are fitted directly in front of the eyepiece.

questions.question: What is the fundamental line in levels?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'The axis of the telescope'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: The axis of the telescope.

questions.question: Which of the statement is correct ?
options: Height of instrument method is more tedious
Rise and fall method is rapid
All checks are made in height of instrument method
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'None of these'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: None of these.

questions.question: The bench mark established by the survey of India department with very high precision with reference to mean sea levelis known as :
questions.explanation: G.T.S. (Great Trigonometrical Survey) Bench Marks are established with very high precision by the Survey of India across the country with reference to Mean Sea Level (MSL) at Mumbai as datum.
questions.rankerTip: GTS = Great Trigonometrical Survey; Datum in India = MSL at Mumbai (formerly Karachi).

questions.question: When it is not possible to set up the level midway between two points, the method of levelling to carry forward thelevels on the other side of the obstruction is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Reciprocal levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Reciprocal levelling.

questions.question: What is the position of line of collimation, if observed staff reading is more than the required true staff reading?
questions.explanation: Standard metric levelling staves are graduated with zero at the base (foot of the staff), so readings increase upwards from bottom to top.
questions.rankerTip: Levelling staves are graduated and read UPWARDS from 0 at the foot.

questions.question: Leveling is the art of finding the ______ of the objects on the surface of the earth
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Relative heights and depths'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Relative heights and depths.

questions.question: A level line is
questions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface concentric with the mean spheroidal surface of the earth, normal to the direction of gravity (plumb line) at every point. A level line is a line lying in a level surface.
questions.rankerTip: Level surface/line is CURVED and concentric with Earth; Horizontal line is STRAIGHT and tangential to level line.

questions.question: Assumed level surface from which vertical measurements are measured is ______
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Datum'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Datum.

questions.question: A fore sight indicate ______ of the instrument
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Shifting instrument'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Shifting instrument.

questions.question: The reduced level of line of collimation is ______ height of instrument
questions.explanation: The Reduced Level of the line of collimation is identical to the Height of Instrument (HI).
questions.rankerTip: Height of Instrument (HI) = Reduced Level of the line of collimation.

questions.question: What is the term for the object seen higher than eye level?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Angle of elevation'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Angle of elevation.

questions.question: For true difference in elevation between 2 points A and B, the level must be set up :
options: At any point between A and B
At exact midpoint of A and B
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'At exact midpoint of A and B'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: At exact midpoint of A and B.

questions.question: Cross sectioning and longitudinal sectioning is:
questions.explanation: Profile levelling (longitudinal sectioning) is carried out along the centerline of a proposed route (road, railway, canal, pipeline) to determine ground undulations and design gradients.
questions.rankerTip: Profile levelling determines elevations along a route alignment to obtain the longitudinal profile.

questions.question: Curvature correction for leveling is always
questions.explanation: Curvature causes points to appear lower than they are, making staff readings too high. Therefore, the curvature correction is always subtractive from staff readings.
questions.rankerTip: Curvature correction is always SUBTRACTIVE; Refraction correction is ADDITIVE; Combined is SUBTRACTIVE.

questions.question: First observation taken on turning point is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Fore sight'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Fore sight.

questions.question: Hypsometry is finding the altitude of various stations by means of a
questions.explanation: Hypsometry determines elevations of high mountain stations based on the variation of boiling point of water with atmospheric pressure, using a hypsometer (thermo-barometer).
questions.rankerTip: Hypsometry = Determining elevation using boiling point of water (thermo-barometer).

questions.question: The stake erected at the required elevation is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Grade stake'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Grade stake.

questions.question: The odd instrument out of the following is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Dumpy level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Dumpy level.

questions.question: Which level is that the line of sight remains horizontal once the operator has roughly levelled the instruments?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Auto level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Auto level.

questions.question: What is the instrument that one person can perform the levelling independently?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Laser level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Laser level.

questions.question: The combined correction due to refraction and curvature is ______ times of curvature correction
questions.explanation: The combined correction is 6/7 times the curvature correction, because refraction correction is 1/7 of curvature correction: (1 - 1/7) * Cc = (6/7) * Cc.
questions.rankerTip: Combined correction = 6/7 of Curvature correction; Refraction correction = 1/7 of Curvature correction.

questions.question: The last staff reading taken before shifting of the level on another position is called :
questions.explanation: A Fore Sight (FS) is the last staff reading taken from an instrument station before shifting the level, or the final sight taken on a point whose elevation is to be determined.
questions.rankerTip: Fore Sight (FS) = Last reading before shifting; Back Sight (BS) = First reading after setting up.

questions.question: An inverted staff reading is taken when the point is :
questions.explanation: An inverted staff reading is taken when the bottom of a structure (such as a bridge girder, tunnel roof, beam soffit, or lintel) is above the instrument line of sight. In level book entries, it is recorded with a negative sign.
questions.rankerTip: Inverted staff reading = Point is ABOVE the line of collimation (entered as negative in level book).

questions.question: In levelling instrument the parallax is wholly eliminated by
options: Placing a shade over the eye piece
questions.explanation: Parallax in a telescope occurs when the real image formed by the objective lens does not lie in the plane of the crosshairs. It is eliminated by: (1) focusing the eyepiece on the crosshairs, and (2) focusing the objective on the staff.
questions.rankerTip: Eliminating parallax: (1) Focus eyepiece on crosshairs against white paper, (2) Focus objective knob on staff.

questions.question: Determining the difference in elevation between two point is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level difference'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level difference.

questions.question: Object of levelling is :
options: To find the elevations of points
To find the bearing of lines
To find the length of lines
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'To find the elevations of points'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: To find the elevations of points.

questions.question: What formula is used in arithmetic check in height of collimation method?
options: ΣB.S - ΣF.S = Last R.L - First R.L
ΣB.S + ΣF.S = Last R.L - First R.L
B.S - F.S = last R.L - First R.L
ΣB.S - ΣF.S = Rise - Fall = Last R.L - First R.L
questions.explanation: In the Height of Collimation method, the arithmetical check is: ΣBS - ΣFS = Last RL - First RL. It does not check intermediate sight calculations.
questions.rankerTip: HI method check: ΣBS - ΣFS = Last RL - First RL.

questions.question: The average refraction correction can be taken as ______ of the curvature correction
questions.explanation: The atmospheric refraction correction is taken as approximately one-seventh (1/7th) of the earth curvature correction.
questions.rankerTip: Refraction correction = 1/7 of Curvature correction = 0.0112 D² m.

questions.question: A Bench mark is a :
options: The last station where the Survey closes
questions.explanation: A Bench Mark (BM) is a fixed reference point of known elevation above a datum, used as the starting and closing point in levelling.
questions.rankerTip: Bench Mark = Relatively permanent point of known elevation.

questions.question: Which column is used, the first entry in the level book page?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Back sight'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Back sight.

questions.question: The type of levelling cannot be done with dumpy level :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Trigonometric levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Trigonometric levelling.

questions.question: One significance of "y level" :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Not rigid in construction'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Not rigid in construction.

questions.question: Reduced level of a point is its elevation with reference to
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Datum'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Datum.

questions.question: In Leveling the effect of refraction is
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends the ray of light downwards, causing the line of sight to intersect the staff lower than a straight line, thus reducing the apparent staff reading.
questions.rankerTip: Refraction bends light downwards -> Reduces staff reading (Correction is ADDITIVE).

questions.question: Which level instrument requires a single permanent adjustment?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Tilting level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Tilting level.

questions.question: The observation with level is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Vertical linear measurement'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Vertical linear measurement.

questions.question: If L is in kilometers, the curvature correction is :
questions.explanation: Curvature correction = D² / (2R) = 0.0785 D² metres (when D is in km), or 78.4 L² mm.
questions.rankerTip: Cc = 0.0785 D² m = 78.4 L² mm (where D or L is in km).

questions.question: An example for a level surface is :
questions.explanation: The still water surface of a calm, tranquil lake or pond represents an authentic level surface, perpendicular to gravity at all points.
questions.rankerTip: Still water surface of a pond/lake = Practical example of a level surface.

questions.question: If a level is in permanent adjustment, its line of collimation is parallel to the axis of the :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Bubble tube'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Bubble tube.

questions.question: What is the name of the staff used while the sights are long and the reading viewed through instrument?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Telescopic staff'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Telescopic staff.

questions.question: The height of instrument is the :
options: Ground level to centre of the telescope
Reduced level of line of sight
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Reduced level of line of sight'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Reduced level of line of sight.

questions.question: An arbitrary surface with reference to which the elevation of points are measured and compared, is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Datum surface'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Datum surface.

questions.question: When levelled, a level provides :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Horizontal line of sight'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Horizontal line of sight.

questions.question: Which survey the longitudinal and cross sections are taken and benchmark is established
questions.explanation: Profile levelling (longitudinal sectioning) is carried out along the centerline of a proposed route (road, railway, canal, pipeline) to determine ground undulations and design gradients.
questions.rankerTip: Profile levelling determines elevations along a route alignment to obtain the longitudinal profile.

questions.question: The line of collimation should be parallel to :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Bubble axis'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Bubble axis.

questions.question: The staff reading taken on a point of known elevation is known as :
questions.explanation: A Back Sight (BS) is the first staff reading taken after setting up the levelling instrument, taken on a point of known elevation (Benchmark or Change Point). It is also called a plus sight.
questions.rankerTip: Back sight (BS) is always the FIRST reading taken from any instrument position and is ADDED to RL to get HI.

questions.question: How many permanent adjustment are required in dumpy level?
questions.explanation: A Dumpy level requires two permanent adjustments: (1) Axis of the level tube must be perpendicular to the vertical axis, and (2) Line of collimation must be parallel to the axis of the level tube.
questions.rankerTip: Dumpy level has 2 permanent adjustments.

questions.question: A relatively fixed point of known elevation is called
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Bench mark'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Bench mark.

questions.question: Which of the following level's telescope can be rotated by surveyor in vertical plane in a smaller amount ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Tilting level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Tilting level.

questions.question: In the rise and fall method of reduction of level, there is check on
questions.explanation: In the Rise and Fall method, the arithmetical check covers: Sum of BS - Sum of FS = Sum of Rise - Sum of Fall = Last RL - First RL, providing a complete check on all readings including intermediate sights.
questions.rankerTip: Rise and Fall check: ΣBS - ΣFS = ΣRise - ΣFall = Last RL - First RL.

questions.question: In telescope the ratio of the focal length of object to that of an eye piece is known as :
questions.explanation: Magnification of a telescope is the ratio of the focal length of the objective lens (F) to the focal length of the eyepiece (f): M = F / f.
questions.rankerTip: Magnification M = Focal length of objective / Focal length of eyepiece.

questions.question: What is reference surface from which elevations are measured?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Mean sea level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Mean sea level.

questions.question: The upper plate of a levelling head of a level is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Tribarch'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Tribarch.

questions.question: How many level screws are used to level the instruments?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Three level screws'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Three level screws.

questions.question: During a fly levelling the plinth of a nearby building is selected as benchmark and its RL is assumed as +50.00. Then the selected BM is an example of
questions.explanation: An Arbitrary (or Assumed) Bench Mark is a reference point whose elevation is arbitrarily assumed (e.g. +100.000 m or +50.000 m) for small, localized levelling operations where actual MSL is not essential.
questions.rankerTip: Arbitrary BM = Assumed datum (e.g. 100.00 m) for localized surveys.

questions.question: The accuracy required in precise levelling is of the order of
questions.explanation: In precise levelling, the permissible closing error is of the order of ± 0.006 √K metres (or ± 6 √K mm).
questions.rankerTip: Precise levelling closing error = ± 0.006 √K m = ± 6 √K mm.

questions.question: How to eliminate parallax between the staff and reticle in auto level?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Turn the focusing knob'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Turn the focusing knob.

questions.question: ______ is a point denoting shifting of the level
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Change point'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Change point.

questions.question: The use of the spirit level fixed to the telescope of a levelling instrument is
options: To make the line of sight vertical
To make the line of sight horizontal
To compute the difference in elevations
To establish the GTS Bench mark
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'To make the line of sight horizontal'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: To make the line of sight horizontal.

questions.question: What is the diameter of earth?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is '12742km'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: 12742km.

questions.question: The method of levelling for determining the difference in elevation of two points either too far apart or obstructed by an intervening ground is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Differential levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Differential levelling.

questions.question: Mean sea level at any place is the average datum of hourly tide height observed over a period of nearly
questions.explanation: Mean Sea Level (MSL) is the average height of the surface of the sea for all stages of tide over a complete 19-year metonic cycle of tidal observations.
questions.rankerTip: MSL is determined by hourly tidal observations averaged over a 19-year period.

questions.question: The process of determining the differences of elevation of stations from vertical angles and known distance is known as
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Trigonometric levelling'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Trigonometric levelling.

questions.question: MSL stands for
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Mean Sea Level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Mean Sea Level.

questions.question: The vertical distance a point above the datum is called ______
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Elevation'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Elevation.

questions.question: The temperature at which water boils is taken as the basis for determining the height of a point is :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Hypsometry'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Hypsometry.

questions.question: BM in surveying designates
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Bench mark'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Bench mark.

questions.question: In levelling, the error due to refraction is
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction varies with temperature and atmospheric conditions throughout the day, acting partially as a compensating error.
questions.rankerTip: Refraction error varies with temperature, time of day, and ground conditions.

questions.question: In precise levelling work, the effect of curvature is that the objects sighted to appear :
questions.explanation: Due to the curvature of the earth, horizontal lines of sight diverge upward from the level surface, making distant objects appear lower than their true level.
questions.rankerTip: Curvature makes objects appear lower than they really are (staff reading increases).

questions.question: In levelling, the correction for refraction (in metres) is equal to
questions.explanation: Refraction correction Cr = (1/7) * 0.0785 D² = 0.0112 D² metres (where D is distance in kilometres).
questions.rankerTip: Refraction correction = 0.0112 D² m (additive to staff reading).

questions.question: What type of works in trigonometric levelling is commonly used?
questions.explanation: Trigonometric levelling is an indirect method of levelling where difference of elevation is computed from observed vertical angles and horizontal distances.
questions.rankerTip: Trigonometric levelling = Elevation difference calculated from vertical angles and distances.

questions.question: In reciprocal levelling
options: A number of readings are taken from a single station
Two set of readings are taken from both end
Repeated readings are taken from both end
Repeated readings are taken from a mid point
questions.explanation: Reciprocal levelling is employed when levelling across wide obstacles (rivers, ravines, lakes) where the instrument cannot be placed midway. Two sets of readings taken from both banks eliminate curvature, collimation, and average refraction errors.
questions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling across rivers eliminates curvature error, collimation error, and uniform refraction error.

questions.question: Mean sea level is a :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Datum'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Datum.
